stem: Disease-like symptoms increase in a dense canopy during repeated periods of high humidity and poor air movement. What is the strongest IPM response?
choices: Assume humidity cannot influence disease pressure
Increase irrigation frequency regardless of root-zone demand
Rely only on removing visibly affected leaves
Evaluate the diagnosis while correcting environmental and canopy conditions that favor disease development, then verify whether incidence changes
rationale: Disease risk depends on the host, causal organism, and environment. Environmental conditions that favor infection or spread are legitimate IPM targets alongside diagnosis and sanitation.
